fact: The UNECA/GIZ/AU Commission inception report dated 19 June 2025 says Mozambique has not enacted a comprehensive data protection law but has drafted a Data Protection Bill, and lists a pending data protection law as a challenge.
The inception report states that Mozambique has no data regulatory authority, though INTIC, INCM, INAGE and CEDSIF impliedly oversee parts of data governance.
The World Bank restructuring paper says that as of October 2025 the Data Protection Act had not been approved by Cabinet or submitted to Parliament, and calls the Data Protection Law still pending.

The World Bank restructuring paper says the Data Protection Office is not yet established, which prevents its operationalisation, and the project envelope for it was cut from US$18m to US$11m; the date is the paper's October 2025 status.

The World Bank and African Development Bank diagnostic of Mozambique's data governance, with evidence updated to spring 2025, refers to the government's preparation of a draft Data Protection Law and recommends that it adopt a data protection law, so none was in force; the document gives no date for the draft, so its 2025-12-09 publication date and spring 2025 evidence cut-off are used.
The statement says the Government approved a proposed Personal Data Protection Law and submitted it to the Assembly of the Republic for consideration.

fact: The Mozambican Assembly's Permanent Commission announced that the plenary is due to consider legislative proposals on personal data protection on 6 November 2026.
